morgan_lee: Hey team — quick sanity check. I ran a bring-up eval comparing model_v4 on our reranker using the human-gold labels vs the synthetic-gold pool we usually use for fast CI. ndcg@10 dropped ~0.018 and mrr ~0.012 when using synthetic golds. wondering if this is an expected gap or a formatting / candidate curation issue. any quick thoughts?
anika_k: Are the candidate pools identical between the two evaluations? synthetic sometimes prunes docs with low-quality html which could change rank distribution.
morgan_lee: Good call — pools came from the same retrieval pass, but synthetic pipeline applies a second heuristics filter (strip duplicates + remove short snippets). I re-ran with identical candidate list and the ndcg gap shrank to 0.006.
samir_r: That suggests curation bias. Do we have slice-level breakdowns? short vs long queries, multi-doc answers?
jin_w: I dumped per-query delta (human - synthetic) and saw heavy tail: 90% of queries within ±0.01, but ~3% have >0.05 loss on synthetic. Those look like "answer spans" buried in long docs where synthetic labeling only kept top snippet.
eval-bot: eval-bot: bootstrap CI (1000 iters) for ndcg@10: human mean=0.682 ±0.003, synthetic mean=0.676 ±0.003, p=0.02.
anika_k: p=0.02 means it's small but consistent. Could be due to synthetic truncation of contexts. Can we try a small ablation: synthetic with full-doc retention but same label heuristics?
morgan_lee: I'll run that. Also want to check tokenizer / whitespace differences that sometimes affect candidate text normalization. Quick command I'm going to run:
```
python eval/rerank_eval.py --gold human --pred model_v4 --metric ndcg@10,mrr --bootstrap 1000 --seed 42 --candidates-file data/candidates/full_doc.jsonl
```
jin_w: Also add --group-by "query_len_bucket" so we can see short/medium/long behavior.
samir_r: FYI, when we brought up v3 we had a small bias because synthetic negatives were sampled closer to query embedding, changing tie frequency — that affected mrr more than ndcg. worth checking sampling distance distribution between pools.
anika_k: Action items: (1) morgan run full-doc synthetic eval (2) jin produce per-query examples for the >0.05 loss queries (3) samir check negative sampling distance histograms. I'll annotate results in the bench PR.
morgan_lee: On it. ETA ~2h, will post the link to the notebook / sample diffs.
jin_w: quick note — let's keep the human-gold and synthetic pipelines' text normalization consistent (casefold/unicode norm). I can add a small wrapper so both evals use same preprocessing path.
morgan_lee: thanks — saving that, and will include the exact command and the seed. If we still see a gap after full-doc + norm parity then we should run a controlled experiment: retrain synthetic labeler variant that preserves long-span matches and re-evaluate.
anika_k: Agree. If the gap persists on controlled experiments we should treat it as a distributional mismatch and prefer human-gold for final gating even if synthetic is fine for fast checks.
eval-bot: eval-bot: created bench run 7023456799 for morgan_lee (link: https://bench/redwood/runs/7023456799)
morgan_lee: Link received, I'll paste results back here when done. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
